utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. The Chamber regrets the late start and I apologise for it. Before we restart with the cross-examination of the witness, the parties have no preliminaries to be raised. The Chamber has delayed its decision on the associated exhibits, but they exceed not a bit but by far the number of the guidance. And apart from the all the technical problems we may have with these associated and exhibits and therefore they should be -- they should be introduced by memorandum so that Madam Registrar is able to see whether everything is uploaded and that the Prosecution has an opportunity to respond to it. But Mr. Lukic, Mr. Stojanovic, you would really have to reconsider. I mean, you rightly complained if there were too many exhibits, we allowed an excess now and then, and -- but always with some limitations. It seems that here you're really flooding the Chamber, and that was exactly what the Chamber did not want to happen. So you're invited to reconsider the number of 61 associated exhibits. If there is nothing else, we could ask the witness to be escorted into the courtroom. I think the Prosecution has some 50 minutes left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Radojcic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would like to remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration you have given at the beginning of your testimony, and Mr. Groome will now continue his cross-examination. Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And good morning, Colonel Radojcic.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can I ask that 65 ter 30891 be brought to our screens.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, Colonel Radojcic, I want to return briefly to the modified air bomb that your brigade fired at Hrasnica on the 7th of April, 1995. I think it will assist the Chamber to see photos of the different locations that you have given evidence about. Can I ask you to take a look at page 1 of this exhibit and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the number. It doesn't reflect --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry. So it's 30891.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now do you agree in the letters A-S mark the location of the Aleksa Santic school -- where the Aleksa Santic school was, the school that was the intended target of the bomb?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now I heard you say "yes," but -- okay, now I see it on the transcript. Now the two towers that are marked by number 1, do you agree that these two residential buildings or high-rise buildings were present during the war?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure. Otherwise, I have to admit that I lived in the inner city of Sarajevo, so I got to know this area just from a distance, as it were.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay, so fair enough. Now the location of the house where the aerial bomb landed has been marked with G10. It is now the site of a hotel. Do you -- does this agree with your recollection of where the aerial bomb landed?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for this place where the bomb fell, nearby there was a small house and it was destroyed by the bomb. And possibly that might be that location, but I cannot be sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to the next page. There's several pictures from different perspectives and perhaps from a different view -- having a different view will assist you. So we'll ignore the towers at number 1 because you're not sure. Again, does A-S indicate where the school is located?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And are you assisted by this view of G10? Does that comport with your recollection of where the bomb landed?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly. But I've already told you that I cannot recognise it because during the war those buildings were not there, the ones that I see here right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. We'll go to one more view.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: If we could go to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I just ask what the witness means by "those buildings were not there ..." To which building did you refer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I mean the buildings that the Prosecutor has indicated. I do not remember. I told you that before the war, I lived in the centre of Sarajevo. And as for Sokolovic Kolonija and Hrasnica, I just know about them from photographs, so I cannot recognise this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This was not my question. You said those buildings were not there. You are referring to the two tall buildings; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. The two tall buildings and other buildings generally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: But you were not asked about these buildings but about the small building where the bomb landed and if you remember that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I thought a little earlier you said you didn't know whether those tall buildings were there before -- during the war or not. Now when you said that they were not there, are you sure that they were not there? Is that -- are you changing your position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've said that I do not know whether they were there. I think they were not there, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. Now we have page 3 of the exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Again, we can see an A-S. Can I ask you to confirm that that is the school, the intended target?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now this view is perhaps the best view of G10 where the Prosecution asserts that the bomb landed. Does this perspective help you recall the precise location of where the bomb landed?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now could we go to page 4 of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, sir, this is a map showing these locations. The Chamber has heard other evidence from Investigator Barry Hogan about the GPS co-ordinates of the location where the bomb landed. So using a computer-based mapping programme, we calculate the distance from the centre of the school to the location the bomb landed to be 150 metres. My question to you is simply do you still maintain your evidence that the bomb fell only 20 metres from the school? You have an opportunity now to change that evidence, if you wish.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not wish to change that evidence. When I say 20, 30 metres away from the school, I got that information from the members of UNPROFOR who were on the spot and who showed me photographs of the place where the bomb landed. So do I not rule out the possibility that this is it, but the information I received was that the bomb had fallen where I had indicated earlier on.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution tenders 65 ter 30891.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 30891 receives number P6618, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could I ask that we go back to page 2 of this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, sir, the next topic I want to ask you about, I want to return to the evidence you gave last week about giving the order to attack an UNPROFOR convoy on Mount Igman on the 14th of July, 1995. Now, if we look at this view of Hrasnica, we can see a mountain behind it. Am I correct that that is Mount Igman?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mount Igman. And we can see that road that we had discussed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. That was my next question. So the road that we can see traversing the mountain, that's the road where the convoy was attacked?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the Igman road, the logistics road as we called it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now I want to the clear up something with respect --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm sorry, can we have 30894 on our screens.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, sir, I want to -- I want to clear up something with respect to the attack that you ordered on the 14th of July. And specifically, I want to read a portion of your testimony last week about it being dark at 6.30 p.m. around the time of the attack and then show you a document.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mladic, no loud speaking. You know what the consequences will be.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You said at transcript page 23248: "I have to mention that at 6.30 p.m. it is not as if one were in The Hague where it is still day-time. At 6.30 p.m. at Igman, it is already dark and one cannot see very well." Now, Colonel Radojcic, what you have on the screen before you is an exhibit which is simply a sunrise-sunset calendar, and there are several such calenders available on the internet, and this particular one is for the city of Sarajevo. And if I can draw your attention to the time of sunset on the 14th, it is circled in red. The letter R indicates the time the sun rose and S the time it set. As we can see, the sunset nearly two full hours after the time you said it was "already dark and one cannot see very well." Again, I ask you whether you stand by your evidence that it was dark at 6.30 p.m. And, again, you have an opportunity to change your evidence at this time, if you wish.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. No, I don't wish to change my evidence because, really, at that time of day, it's dark at Igman because this road goes through the forest and the sun sets earlier there. And, quite simply, from the distance from which we were targeting, you cannot see clearly. So I stand by what I said. UNPROFOR withdrew their own forces into their bases at 1800 hours precisely for that reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. Can I ask that we go to the next page. And this is the same calender for July of this year, 2014. And we can see that in 12 days the sun will set at exactly the same time, 2027 hours and 14 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: If I were to make arrangements for an investigator stationed in Sarajevo, if you're discharged as a witness in this case, would you accompany the investigator to where you say it was dark two hours before sunset? Would you do that 12 days from now?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay, fair enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honours, Prosecution tenders Exhibit -- 65 ter 30894.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: We would object, Your Honours. There has been no foundation laid for whether these are estimates or actual times. Based upon the last page, it would appear these were estimates done in advance, not on the actual circumstances of the day. So I don't think there has been evidence lead, apart from Mr. Groome's comments, to identify the document and how it was generated.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would simply say that astronomy is one of our oldest and most certain sciences. I've included the reference at the bottom of the exhibit that certainly it can be verified. If the Chamber wishes to give Mr. Ivetic an opportunity to verify it, I'd ask that it be marked for identification and he can investigate whether, in fact, these --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What do you mean by "estimates or actual times," Mr. Ivetic, in this respect?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, July 14th of 2014 has not yet occurred, so it's not known whether on the actual day what the atmospheric conditions have been.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: -- so if the other --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, are you serious about that you expect all estimates on what will happen on the 14th of July as far as sunset and sunrise is concerned would be considerably different from what we find in these kind of tables? I mean, estimates is not being certain about it. You'd say it could be one minute later or earlier or is that ... I just don't understand your --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, I know that things can vary in astronomy and atmospheric conditions, and that's what my concern is that we're getting into something where we're speculating, that we don't know. I'm not an astronomer to be able to give you evidence; neither is Mr. Groome. Therefore --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But the first -- the first day, of course, was from the past. That has happened already, and --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And we don't know whether it was an estimate, like these others are, or whether it was an actual recording. That's my point, Your Honour. Based upon this exhibit that shows the same data for a date in the past and a date in the future, we don't know whether they're estimates or actual recordings after the fact. And that's my objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, could I inquire --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could I inquire of Mr. Ivetic if I produced a calendar that showed that for every year for the last 20 years since 1995 the sun set at the same time on the 14th of July, would he be satisfied that it will, in fact, set at that time 12 days from now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The objection is denied. Mr. Ivetic, if there is something happening on the 14th of July of this year which changes the -- I would say the constant and precise recording of sunset and sunrise, you may revisit the matter. Madam Registrar, the number would be.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 30894 receives number P6619, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could I ask that we now go to 65 ter 1D02134. And this is a document dated the 11th of September, 1993, and entitled: "Orders, Decision on Disciplinary measure."

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Colonel Radojcic, while that's being brought to our screens, in several places in your statement, you assert your commitment to enforcing good discipline among your subordinates. I want to explore this with you now, and I want to begin by asking you about some of the specific events you recount in your statement. You speak about the document our on screen now in paragraph 74 of your statement. And to save time, I will summarise your evidence and ask you whether you agree. As I understand this decision, it was signed on your behalf by your chief of staff, and in it you sentenced a soldier by the name of Sretan Crkvenjas to 40 days of military detention. You sentenced him to detention because, on 10 September 1993, he and another soldier in a drunken state forced their way into the communications room where this soldier called another officer, Nenad Perisic, on the phone, threatened him, and demanded he come to where they were. When Perisic came to that location, Crkvenjas assaulted him. Have I correctly summarised the factual finds or factual -- facts that you established -- or were established regarding this event?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: This matter was investigated and dealt with within a 24-hour period; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was Perisic a superior officer to Crkvenjas?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I so assume. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can we go to the next page in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And could we actually go to the last page in the original, if we could.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now am I correct that Crkvenjas signed this decision and doing so was acknowledgement of it and that he accepted his punishment?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you ever have any problems with Crkvenjas after this?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Would this event and your punishment of Crkvenjas have been known to other soldiers in the brigade?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In principle, all punishment that is meted out by the commander of the brigade down the chain of command reaches each and every soldier, and there are certain lessons drawn on the basis of that punishment.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now what do you think the impact on the brigade would have been if Crkvenjas had assaulted Perisic and there had been no punishment or no action taken?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Quite simply, such an incident could not have gone by unpunished, so every incident of this nature was punished more or less in the same way.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I guess what I'm getting at, if you had not taken such quick and decisive action, is there a likelihood that other soldiers would have thought that they could have assaulted officers and do so without being held to account for having done so?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now could we please call up 1D02008. And this is a document entitled: "Order on a disciplinary measure," dated 26 of July, 1993. Signed by Colonel Radojcic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And you deal with this in paragraph 132 of your statement. While that's being brought to your screens, perhaps you remember this case. In this case on the 26th of July, 1993, you ordered 60 days of military detention for a soldier by the name of Novak Popadic. He did several things including the most serious of which was he fired a zolja hand-held rocket launcher at ambulance at 8.30 on the morning of the 26th. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did he ever --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Groome can you repeat the number of the document for the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm sorry. 1D02008.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did the ambulance belong to the 1st Battalion of your brigade?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now obviously firing a hand-held rocket at an ambulance was a very serious breach of discipline. Am I correct in concluding that you were able to effectively investigate and take corrective action with respect to this incident within a very short period of time?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Am I correct in thinking that if you had not taken such quick and decisive disciplinary action, such a failure might have encouraged other members of the brigade to act in an undisciplined away, including misusing their weapons?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now could I ask that 1D02148 be brought to our screens.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And it is a document that you discuss in paragraph 94 of your statement. And, again, I see your statement at your right hand, so please feel free to look at it if it assists you. It's a document entitled: "Report about violation of armistice by Ilidza brigade," dated 21 August 1993 and signed by Deputy Commander Dragomir Milosevic. The next matter I would like to address with you relates to an order your brigade received to investigate two separate allegations that the VRS had broken a cease-fire on the 17th of August, 1993. And, again, you address this in paragraph 94. Colonel, at the outset, my primary focus is not the substance of the event but the procedure that was followed, and I want to be sure that I fully understand this procedure. I want to go through a series of three documents associated with your statement and ask you very specific questions. My first question is: One of the allegations was that on 17 August 1993 at 1530 hours two T-55 tanks from the Ilidza Brigade opened fire on an UNPROFOR transport.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what is written in this document. However, as far as I can remember, at this time I was not in the area of responsibility of the brigade, and it was the chief of staff of the brigade that stood in for me. So I cannot say anything specific about this currency.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. And, again, I'm not interested in the substance but the procedure. The second alleged breach of the cease-fire concerned a mortar being fired from the Nedzarici Brigade into Dobrinja at about 1940 hours in which 40 victims were said to be injured; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is what is written in this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now I want to go to two other documents, but before we leave this document, I just want you to note --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: If we could go back to the first page in both documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I want you to note at this moment that this report of what happened on the 17th of August was sent to the Main Staff on the 21st of August and bears the reference number 20/15-944/3, okay?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now if we can go --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: If we can go to 1D02526.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And this is order 20/15-944, dated the 18th of August, 1993, marked "top urgent." Now, Colonel Radojcic, can you take a look at this document. In this document on the 18th of August, 1993, the commander of the SRK, Stanislav Galic, orders you to urgently investigate the reasons fire was opened from two Ilidza Brigade tanks on an UNPROFOR transport; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. However, at that point, I was not in the area of responsibility of the brigade. I was visiting my family, so I'm not familiar with --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. Do you agree with me that this document is related to the report that we just looked at a minute ago? It is the order to investigate which then resulted in the report?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could we now look at 65 ter 1D02152.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, this is an urgent order from Stanislav Galic ordering an investigation. It is dated the 20th of August, 1993. Again, we see the reference number 20/15-944, followed by a 2. Once again, it is an order to the Ilidza Brigade to investigate something. In this case, an allegation by UNPROFOR that on 17 August 1993 at 1940 hours there was mortar fire from Nedzarici over Dobrinja allegedly injuring 14 people; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what is written in this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now the second paragraph states: "With regard to the Order of the General Staff, classified number 17/230-380 of 19.08.1993 form a Commission and investigate the incident in order to review all the circumstances regarding the place, reason, and participants, and a battle situation during the action." This document indicates that the Main Staff issued an order on 19 August for this event to be investigated; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And do you agree with me again, this is an order -- or these are the documents that are related to that report that was ultimately sent to the Main Staff about these -- these two events?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now you refer to this particular document in paragraph 100. And you say: "The UN observers' problem was that they had one or two observers in our area of responsibility and they covered a vast area and could not have an overview of our brigade's actions." As I understand your evidence, at any given time there were no more than two UNPROFOR observers within the entire area of responsibility of the Ilidza Brigade; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, at the time. There were either two or three, depending on the time. They had their base, and from that base, they went to different areas, depending on what the needs were.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So it's your evidence that it was impossible for them to see everything, in essence?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they couldn't observe everything basically.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now I'd like to return to the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And that's 1D02148.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And this is the report that went to the Main Staff on the 21st of August, 1993 and signed by Deputy Commander Dragomir Milosevic. Now we can see from the first line of the report that the Main Staff issued two orders to investigate these two allegations. One was order 17/230-377 on 17 August, and the other was 17/230-380 on 20 August 1993; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now if we look at item 1, second paragraph, we see in that, that it is a response to the Main Staff order -- I'm sorry, that in response to the Main Staff order the SRK issued its own order, and that's order number 15/20-944; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to suggest to you that there has been a typo here, and this is really a reference to the earlier documents 20/15-944. Would you agree with my interpretation that the typist of this document inadvertently reversed the 20 and the 15?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. The next paragraph summarises the results of the investigation; correct? And, again, I'm not interested so much in the substance, but here we have a summary of the facts that were established in this investigation; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now turning to item 2, again we see the report indicates the SRK order assigning persons to investigate the matter and then summarises the findings of the investigation; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now the purpose of this document or this report is to inform the Main Staff of the results of this investigation that they ordered; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now the report to the Main Staff is dated 21st of August, 1993. Again, recognising that you were on family leave, is it your view that this event could be adequately investigated and reported on within four days, this relatively brief period of time?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the text we can see what happened and there is an explanation. The very fact that certain measures were taken testifies to the fact that the reaction was immediate.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So I want to now see if I understand the procedure and the capacities. So what we've just gone with these three documents, that indicates that the Main Staff of the VRS had the capacity and the means to conduct detailed investigations into matters related to actions of soldiers; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was there any period of time during your tenure as commander of the Ilidza Brigade that you came to learn that the Main Staff did not have this capacity?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Main Staff learned of all incidents first and foremost through the chain of command and also through UNPROFOR liaison officers, as well as liaison officers with the command of the SRK who were in direct communication with the corresponding organs of the Main Staff. These two bodies provided quick access for General Mladic to all information taking place in the area of activity of each of the brigades, individually.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And similarly we saw a few minutes ago, you had your own ability as commander of the brigade to initiate investigations into breaches of discipline; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did have the possibility of launching an investigation. As for the explanation provided here by the SRK Command to the Main Staff, one can clearly see what actually happened. The incident is explained, and in this first incident where the -- there was alleged firing by the two T-55 tanks, the assertion is that our tanks did not open fire as they were close to the command. The UNPROFOR vehicle was close to the Luzani settlement. Let me remind you, Luzani --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- is the most densely populated area in --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Again, I'm focusing --

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: -- on the procedure not so much the substance of it. So now I want to turn -- what we understand now, and now let's turn our attention to G8 and your evidence about that. And G8 is the first shelling of the Markale market, and it occurs about six months after this event. In paragraph 108, you that General Milosevic ordered you to "establish the facts about the shell," and this is in reference, of course, to the first shelling of Markale. I see you're going through your statement. Okay. You have it. Now the Defence has not tendered through you any similar documentation that we've just seen, and I know of none in our collections. So my question to you is: Do you have in your possession any report similar to the one we have just looked at with respect to your efforts to establish the facts of the first shelling of Markale?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pursuant to an order by General Mladic, the Chief of the Main Staff, General Galic or General Milosevic was tasked to urgently establish a commission that would co-operate with UNPROFOR in order to attend the scene and check the circumstances under which the Markale I incident took place. I was a member of the three-member commission. I was taken by an UNPROFOR vehicle across the --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- airport runway, and I spent the next 24 hours --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: -- I'm very pressed for time. So my question is simply: Are you in possession of any documentation similar to what we've just seen, with respect to Milosevic's order to you to establish the facts of Markale, the first shelling of Markale? Are you in possession of any documentation like that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no such documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not supposed to go there because of any documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, earlier you made a reference to paragraph 8 of the statement where it might be that you intended to refer to 108.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now in paragraph 25 of your statement, you say that it was absolutely never your intention to terrorise civilians and never knew members of your unit, as well as superior and subordinate units to terrorise civilians. I'm going to ask that you look at a document with me; it's P6523. And it's a document entitled: "Conclusions and tasks from a briefing at SRK Command, on 31 March, 1994," dated 1st of April, 1994. Now, Colonel, this -- well, we'll give it a moment to come up. This is a list of 31 tasks assigned to members of the SRK by Major-General Galic. I want to draw your attention to number 8.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And that can be found on the second page of the English, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Where it says: "Fortify positions, around Sarajevo by erecting wire and concrete barriers which would, in turn, strengthen the belief that they are really are blocked ('in a camp')." Now my first question to you is: Do you think that -- I mean, we know that Serb civilians were kept in detention facilities. Do you think that Serb civilians kept in a detention facility would have experienced feelings of vulnerability, fear, perhaps even terror? Would you acknowledge that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I may, I would like to study this entire document. I am not certain what it is all about and I could provide a better answer after that. Based on your question --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- I can only state that --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: -- if that's what you want to do, I am sure that the Chamber won't object to you having a chance to look at that document. So perhaps we will do that, and perhaps I'd be granted the opportunity to ask that question after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if a copy of the document could be given to the witness so that he could have a look at it during the break. Perhaps, Madam Registrar, you could make a print-out of this document which consists of --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could I ask that now P6513 be brought to our screens.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And this is an order signed by Dragomir Milosevic on the 21st of July, 1995. It's addressed to several subordinate units of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps, including the Ilidza Brigade. And my first question to you is: Do you recall receiving this order?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And I can see here that it wasn't signed by General Milosevic. It was signed by a certain Dragicevic on his behalf.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, in this order we read: Our forces on the Trnovo axis who have a lot of problems (Kragujevac, Cardak, Hum, Celina have fallen) on top of all other difficulties, our defence on Mount Treskavica also has a lot of problems. The Turks have probably moved the main focus of attack towards Gorazde in order to relieve our forces on the Trnovo axis and to link up the forces and deceive the enemy, I hereby order. In this order, Milosevic is referring to problems that VRS troops outside the theater of Sarajevo are experiencing; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now the first order reads: "The brigade commands shall independently plan, prepare, and carry out an attack or a show attack against the city of Sarajevo..." Now, sir, this is an order to attack the city of Sarajevo. So my first question to you is, is: As a brigade commander, did you implement this order as it applied to you?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The order was not sent to my brigade alone. If you look at the header, it was sent --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- to the Ilidza Brigade --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: -- I certainly appreciate that. But my question is limited to, you did receive the order. Did you implement it as it pertained to you? Did you take any action in response to this order?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time I was at the forward command post at Nisici where the corps command was. I did learn of this order but I wasn't familiar with its details. The chief of staff stood in for me while I was absent.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Well, sir, do you acknowledge that this order orders an attack or a show attack on the town of Sarajevo in response to events that are happening in other parts of the -- of the country?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is how the order was drafted. I acknowledge that. But it contains another thing, all of us, the brigade commanders, were familiar with the position and the order of the chief of Main Staff for the city of the Sarajevo not to be taken at any point during the war and that it would be left to politics to deal with it after the war. This order was just to demonstrate that position and to tie down the 1st Corps forces to our units and to enable freer movement for our forces in the Trnovo theater.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution tenders P6513. It is now marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It has a number already. I missed that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So it's P6513, MFI'd.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And is now admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, last week at T-23213, I asked you to describe the sound of a modified air bomb, the sound that it made as it travelled through the air. And you said: "It created quite a terrifying sound, because during its flight and due to the emission of powder gases, one could hear a very strong hiss." Now you experienced the sound as a terrifying sound and you knew that it was moving away from you. Do you accept that the people in Sarajevo, hearing that sound passing over their heads or towards their location, would also have experienced the sound as a terrifying one?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose so.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now when you fired the one -- the air bomb at Hrasnica, were you able to hear that sound the entire journey of the projectile to where it landed?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember whether I could hear it throughout its trajectory, but in the first stage of its flight I certainly did.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. Now the last set of questions I want to ask you is about an associated exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And it's 1D02153.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And while that's being brought to our screens, can I ask you who Dragan Marcetic was?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dragan Marcetic was the chief of staff of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps in 1993. Once he left, General Milosevic assumed the position who, at the time, was still a colonel.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now this document is authored --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, I'm looking at the clock, and I'm also informed that you have used your full six hours. How much time would you still --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I just have a few questions on this document and this is the last document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that's the last document.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: That's it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I suggest that we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Since we had a late start we can continue for a couple of minutes and have a bit of a later break.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So this document is authored by Dragan Marcetic and it's dated the 12th of June, 1993 and entitled "Artillery fire and mortar fire over urban parts of Sarajevo." Now, Colonel Radojcic, you provided evidence about this document in paragraph 103 of your statement. And you say: "My comment is the same the one for 1D8390." And now as far as I can figure, and I informed Mr. Ivetic of this last week, you do not comment on 1D8390 in your statement. So I'm going to ask you -- would you please read the first four paragraphs of this order and then I want to ask you a question about it. So if you can read it out loud and so it can be translated because the translation is somewhat problematic. Could you just read it and we'll read along in English but perhaps we may have a more precise understanding.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the heading, it states that it is to deal with the opening of artillery fire on urban parts of Sarajevo: "Caution: "Forward to all SRK commanders and to the rear command post to commander personally. "Despite several orders and caution issued by the SRK Commander not to open fire from bigger calibre weapons on Sarajevo, it is still being done. Certain Commanders, especially in battalions and regiments, violate this order wilfully issued by the SRK Commander disregarding the consequences. "We all care to do away with as many Turks as possible, but not at the expense of such political consequence caused by a couple of shells or mines in Sarajevo with minimum effect. "I caution unit commanders that criminal proceedings will be instituted against irresponsible and wilful officers. All officers and soldiers need to be explained the consequences of such irresponsible and wilful conduct. "Preserving ammunition is the task number one. Our sources of supply have dried up. Ammunition cannot be obtained. "Explain to the soldiers and officers to open fire only upon order and approval of superior officers and only against clearly visible targets and when strictly required to do so. Recalcitrant and irresponsible soldiers and officers shall be called to task and submit reports against them in order to conduct proceedings and establish their criminal responsibility. "Deputy Commander, Dragan Marcetic." I just want to add that this order was sent to all SRK units and not only to my unit; thus, it means that it wasn't -- it wasn't only my units which violated the cease-fire and opened fire on Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay, sir, I'm interested now in the second paragraph, and it uses the word "poturica," and do you agree that that term "poturica" is a derogatory term for Muslims which literally means a person who started life as a non-Muslim but then became one. Do you agree that that's the literal definition of the phrase that's used by Marcetic?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On top of this term, there are quite a few others used by commanders unfortunately. For example, in the previous one --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- the word was "turci," similar to this one. So it's obvious that -- well, in principle, the term was used for people who converted to Islam despite their ethnic background having been Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So, sir, in hindsight as you sit here today, in 2014, do you consider it appropriate for a senior officer in the VRS to say something like this in an order, and it's been translated, "We all care to do away with as many Turks as possible." As you sit here today, do you consider that an appropriate thing for a senior officer to have in an order?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is very complicated to provide an answer to this question, but in principle I never used such terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So do I take it that you agree, as you sit here, that this is inappropriate, to find something like this in an order from a senior officer of the VRS?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'd rather not comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you agree that its plain meaning to soldiers on the black and white is that: Despite your wish to liquidate all "poturica," we must conserve our ammunition. That's what's being communicated here on its face; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is a rather unfortunate order. It is not skillfully drafted and basically every sentence of it could be commented on. The fact is, though -- well, you can even see that some parts of it are contradictory: Do away with as many and yet be very careful with spending ammunition.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, does the fact that this language could be you used by a high-ranking VRS officer in a written order suggest that Marcetic believed that his superiors would not object to the use of some language?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There would certainly be no objections because we were also called by the ABiH army different names. I'd rather not go into that because some of them are far worse than this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So it is true that Marcetic used such offensive language without reservation because the army that General Mladic had created was an army in which senior officers --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mladic is supposed to be seated. If he wants to consult with counsel, he has an opportunity to do so at a volume inaudible for anyone else.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Marcetic -- I put to you that Marcetic felt that he could use such language in an order to his subordinates because the army created by General Mladic was an army in which senior officers could openly talk and write about murdering Muslims and have no fear of disciplinary action being taken against them. Is that not true?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably. This -- had this order been sent to the Main Staff as well, it wouldn't have been drafted like this. All I can say is that I never used terms like this in my orders. I would always use the term "B and H army members."

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Colonel Radojcic, that's all the questions I have. I do want to thank you for answering so many questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Groome. We'll first take a break. Could the usher, apart from escorting the witness out of the courtroom, provide the witness with a copy of the statement -- or a copy of the document he asked to further review. Mr. Ivetic, you're on your feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was hoping to bring to your attention the document that we just saw on the screen. The English, obviously as we all saw, had some errors, among them the name of the officer who signed it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Apart from the other matter that sometimes -- apparently the translation "Turks," which Mr. Groome used when reading and which was -- we received through interpretation today, is apparently dealt with on an equal footing with those converted to -- into Islam, not T Islam, but to Islam, and there were many, many others mistakes. So I think that it would be wise to have the document we had last on our screen to be reviewed. I don't know who prepared the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, we had those concerns when we read it. We've asked CLSS to do that. I will ask Ms. Stewart to forward that document, the CLSS official translation of this document to Mr. Ivetic, and leave it to Mr. Ivetic then to perhaps replace the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you did read from that --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I read from the -- what the translated -- what the booth did. I just read from the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, from the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I didn't read from that document. I'll leave it to the Mr. Ivetic to see whether he agrees with CLSS about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That explains why the word "Turks" appeared again, different from what --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes. I didn't want to use a different word than had been translated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, it will be taken care of. Could the witness be escorted out of the courtroom. We take a break of 20 minutes. After that, some re-examination may follow. And you are provided with the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We take a break and will resume at five minutes past 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, I'm just wondering, since the witness now has been given an opportunity to review that document, whether - and I'm also looking at Mr. Ivetic - if you have one or two questions whether you want to put them now or we would -- yes, I see Mr. Ivetic would not oppose if you do it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think I made the point that I wanted to do without it, but certainly if the witness has a comment that he thinks might assist the Chamber, I have no objections. So maybe I'll simply ask him --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Is there any comment that you wish to make about the document that you've seen?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: That's P6523.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And the portion that I had drawn your attention to was paragraph 8.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's a general order of 31 paragraphs. It's generally imprecise, and I really wouldn't want to comment on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Perhaps then we leave it there then, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We leave it there. Mr. Radojcic, Mr. Ivetic will now put questions to you in re-examination. Mr. Ivetic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Good day again, Colonel. I'd like to first return to the issue of semi-encirclement and paragraph 5 of your statement, D535.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Page 2 in the English and page 3 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, in this paragraph, you say that the only communication our brigade had with the rest of Republika Srpska was through Rajlovac. And I'd like to ask you how wide or how narrow was the area, you know, of this communication by way of Rajlovac?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps 10 kilometres as the crow flies. The B and H army on one side and on the other side the Croatian Defence Council.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And did either the ABiH army on the one side or the Croatian Defence Council on the other side have ability to fire upon this communication route?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At certain points, the road was some 50 to 100 metres close. For example, the entrance to the Pretis factory was 50 metres away from Muslim positions. It was very unsafe to move around. We had to put up shields for protection. As for the Croatian Defence Council, they never created any problems for us while we were using that corridor.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, in the statement and in the answers that you gave during cross-examination, you kept using the term "communication." Could you define for us what, in layman's terms, in layperson terms, what is meant in the former Yugoslav military as a communication or a "komunikacija"?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Komunikacija," it's a general term for moving on land, sea, and area. In this case, it's land roads and the network of land roads.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. And now you've identified that the ABiH did fire upon this area. What kind of weaponry did the ABiH utilise to fire upon this area of this communication?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most frequently they used rifles, semi-automatic and automatic rifles. They didn't use snipers because, in that area, there was no need for that kind of fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And were casualties incurred by your troops in this area of Rajlovac, this communication of Rajlovac?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that the Ilidza Brigade had any casualties while moving along that road.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now I'd like to move on. In one of the prior days, at transcript page 23122, lines 8 through 15, you were asked by Judge Orie about the procedure for taking follow-up shots with a mortar to destroy a target. The question I have for you: Is there always a need to destroy a target to consider a mission successful?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are two terms in military terminology: To neutralise a target and to destroy a target. What we're talking about the first term, neutralising a target, then the weapon and the ammunition expenditure is noted and the purpose is not to destroy but to throw it out of action for a certain period of time. When there is an order to destroy a target, there is no limit to the ammunition that can be used and the target is destroyed completely. So these two targets were used to neutralise or destroy a target. It's up to the commander to evaluate the weapons he will use. He would use those weapons which would, in the quickest and most efficient way, destroy or neutralise a given target.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And I'd like to raise another matter raised this time by Mr. Groome, at transcript page 23138, when he said that the Plamen rocket put in a launch tube was analogous to a bullet being put in a chamber of a long-barreled weapon and being fired. Now, as an infantryman, could you focus for a moment on an infantry rifle and could you describe for us the inside surface of the rifle tube?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm an infantry officer but not an artillery officer, but I can answer your question. But if you can just repeat exactly what it is that you want to know.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The interior of a rifle tube, could you describe that for us?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The interior of a rifle tube has four grooves and four fields. They are slightly curved as you move from the chamber of the bullet towards the mouth of the barrel, and that is how you provide the rotation of the bullet and additional stability while it is flying towards its target.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can I just inquire whether there is any dispute about the, at least inadequacy on this point, about the tube and a rifle - how do you call it? - because rotation is typically for a rifle bullet to be done and that's not the same with tubes for rockets, is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I certainly agree with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Although --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There seems to be no disagreement that the comparison is not accurate in this respect but is mainly about being in a tube of wider or lesser, but the difference I would have been surprised if there would have been any dispute about it, whether this is not --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And also, my recollection is that the witness said that the mortar tube is the more relevant example and then I abandoned any discussion of a rifle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And the mortar tube, I think the parties agree on that as well, does not have any grooves and fields.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Correct. And that was what the Prosecution --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No rotation --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: -- the witness testified to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now I'd like to return with you to the topic of video which was played by Mr. Groome the other day. It was at transcript 23145 and onwards and was admitted over my objection as Exhibit P6614. In that video, we saw the name of the 21st Sabotage Detachment. Have you ever heard of any unit of the VRS that has been called by that designation?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I must admit that I did not hear much about that unit. I know that there was a sabotage detachment, but I didn't know about this particular one.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now in the video that was shown, there were the names of certain military operations flashed on the screen, including Grude 77. Have you ever heard of any VRS military action labelled or called Grude 77?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And there was another name, Spreca 94. Have you ever heard of a VRS military action called Spreca 94?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Was the army of the Serb Krajina, according to your understanding, a formational element of the VRS?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was never part of it, and there was never any direct link between those two armies.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, a search of the internet by myself encountered the whole video, not the edited portion presented by the Prosecution. I've asked for a stipulation from the Prosecution that the video, indeed, refers to another army in another theater of war, not the VRS. I have not yet received a response. I just wanted to bring that to your attention. Depending to the results of that, I may seek to tender the entire video once a transcript is prepared of the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic has not provided me with this video. If he does, I'll look at it. I'm happy to consider any offer he may wish to make regarding it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I would direct counsel to his e-mail where the link for video on YouTube was provided.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And I responded to that this morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And I said I do not have access to YouTube.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: YouTube is a prohibited area for the --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: For all of us, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- for those working in this Tribunal, Mr. Ivetic, as you may know.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'll be happy to provide that to Mr. Groome at the next break. I have it on USB.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that would be -- and could you also -- we had some experience with some sources which were perhaps not always extremely reliable on videos, the presentation of videos. Does it originate from the same source as the video we've seen in relation with Mr. -- what was his name --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Vulliamy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It does not come from the same source as I believe that was 1D44 or thereabouts. And I found multiple sources with the same video --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: -- that also identify it as being another army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would say at this stage I only offered it based on Colonel Radojcic's evidence that it was similar for that purpose. The Chamber admitted on that limited basis, that it showed a similar device. So I'm happy to agree at this stage that the sound and the titles be ignored by the Chamber as the witness did not give evidence about them. If that solves the problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'm only asking for a stipulation. I'm not asking for any substantive evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand you're only asking for a stipulation. Mr. Groome was unable to open it, and Mr. Groome says apparently the issue why you're asking for a stipulation is not the issue on which the Prosecution relies in this respect. So, therefore, what Mr. Groome more or less offers is that -- to create a situation in which the stipulation might lose its importance. And if you --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: -- this video was used with another witness, a protected witness, and questions were asked of that witness implying that this was a VRS weapon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It -- my recollection is not such that I could either at this moment --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I don't know the pseudonym of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What I suggest is the following: Mr. Groome looks at the video and you consider whether the issue would be in full or in part be resolved by the offer Mr. Groome made. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now I wish to turn to the topic of the so-called Plamen launcher.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if we could please turn to Exhibit P6616 in e-court, at transcript page 23148. Oh, I'll wait for the picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Groome pointed to this picture labelled as the Plamen launcher and asked you if it was the Plamen launcher and you said yes. Now --

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did your brigade have this particular weapon system in your heavy weapons arsenal? And now I'm talking about the weapons system depicted in the photograph.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we did not have Plamen in any shape or form.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with a weapons platform or weapon called the M-77 Oganj, O-g-a-n-j?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only from photographs and shooting practice, otherwise no.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Are you able to describe for us any of the main differences between the M-77 Oganj which differentiated from M-63 Plamen, especially in relation to the ammunition used.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This Plamen rocket launcher has 32 rockets, and Oganj, I think, has 16. They are longer range and heavier charge rockets and have a greater effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I would like to call up alongside this Prosecution photo image 1D7031.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And I would ask: Does the upper right photograph appear to be the identical vehicle as we just saw in the Prosecution's photograph that we just looked at, P6616?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now this web page identifies this weapons system as M-77 Oganj. Do you permit that you and perhaps Mr. Groome did not look closely at the photo when identifying it as a Plamen launcher?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I would now like to call up alongside the Prosecution image P6616, 1D7030.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm seeing all of these for the first time. Has Mr. Ivetic given us notice of these documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I believe the procedure during the Prosecution case was that we found out about redirect documents that arose out of cross-examination at the time they were presented. I do not recall having received them. I can tell you that they're all photographs that I was able to find on the internet following Mr. Groome's cross-examination. I can give you the numbers of all the photographs that I wish to use. There's only, I think, two more.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: That's okay. I'll look at them for the first time when they come up on our screens.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Please proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, looking at the photograph on the right, which is 1D7030, this appears similar to the photograph on the left except that the launch tubes are much smaller. Do you recognise this system from the arsenal of either the JNA or the VRS? And when I say "this system," I'm talking about the picture on the right.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is the Plamen system.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if we can then --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I don't think I need to show you the next picture since you have recognised it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If I can pull up 1D7032. And if we could zoom in on the top-right photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, this purports to be the M-63 Plamen VBR 128. Now I'd ask you to look at the first image and tell me if you can confirm that this does accurately depict the rockets when they are loaded into the Plamen system, in this case a wheeled version not a turreted version.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were several versions. We see the M-63 version here on its mobile platform installed with two rockets ready to fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And is it correct that the rockets, when ready to fire, actually protrude from the launch tube as is depicted in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it means that they were placed into the tube and that they are ready to fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And this type of rocket-launch system, can you tell us if you recall this as being a weapon that was within either the JNA or the VRS arsenal?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were weapons in the Yugoslav Peoples' Army. And, as I said, they were placed in operational units. Not tactical units. As far as I know, they were part of the corps and army artillery pieces.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And this particular version on the top right of this page, does it appear to have an axle of the type that you and Mr. Groome discussed yesterday in cross-examination, or turret?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see a turret here, specifically. But I can see a handle that can be turned and that is how you would move the system from left to right and by height. I don't see a turret here.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can zoom out, I think there is other photographs. I don't know that any of them actually assist except that maybe the fourth from the top.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Does this view help you to determine if there is a turret for this particular multi-rocket launcher system?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you're thinking about the part that makes it possible to move the system left and right and up and down, then it's there. But if you think of some -- if you're thinking of something else, then I don't see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. I was thinking of -- in terms of --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can have again P6616 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: When I'm using the word "turret," I'm referring to the part that is identified by Mr. Groome's red arrow.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I don't think that that part is called a turret. It has a different name because a turret would be placed above the system, not below. Since I don't know what that part is called precisely, we can define it as a system ensuring that the system is moved left and right and up and down.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Fair enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if we can go back to 1D7032.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And perhaps I can ask the question this way: Do you recall what the length of a Plamen rocket was from its head to its tail? In approximation. It doesn't have to be exact.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, maybe 70 or 90 centimetres. Perhaps more than that. I cannot say. I don't really know.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, the witness redefines the -- what Mr. Groome introduced. I understood Mr. Groome, when he was talking about the turret, irrespective of whether that's the right name or not, to refer to a system which would allow for horizontal movement. Not vertical movement. But since the witness now has redefined it, I'd like to verify with Mr. Groome whether he simply used the kind of, if I could say, a kind of a circular system which allows for horizontal movement. Perhaps even up to 360 degrees but turn in every direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. So when I used the word "turret," I meant the horizontal left to right movement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And I think the Chamber will recall Colonel Radojcic talking about the pistons that accounted for the up and down movement. I'd also note that just reading the text here apparently all of these have traverse movement and up and down elevation movement despite whether or not we can see them, so I'm wondering the purpose of these questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, we leave that in the hands of Mr. Ivetic for the time being. Mr. Ivetic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The document states the Plamen rocket is 0.814 metres long. Does that correspond to your recollection, sir?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, could I ask the witness a question, apart from how leading your previous question was, you give us details up to the -- up to the millimetre what is your recollection of the Plamen rocket. But in your previous testimony, you were not even able to identify what was a Plamen rocket or not because apparently you were mistaken when you confirmed that what was shown to you by Mr. Groome that that was or was not a Plamen rocket. What explains your detailed knowledge about these weapons systems where last, when was it, Thursday or Friday, you were not even able to identify the systems shown to you correctly. And looking at the pictures now, they are really not the same. They are quite different. What is it that you -- made it unable for you to identify them last week and why you can even tell us up to the millimetre at this moment the measurements of the system shown to you now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, even now I cannot say exactly to the millimetre. I said 70 to 90 centimetres. And it is Mr. Ivetic who gave this information in millimetres, .814. So I stand by what I said. My understanding is that what is accentuated here is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You were asked when the measurement was given to you by the millimetre, does that correspond to your recollection, sir. Now I do now understand from your answer that you say it's more or less in line with what I remember but don't ask me about details. That's not what you said. You said yes. So you just confirmed it. But even if it's not up to the millimetre, you are not able even to recognise -- to identify what was shown to you by Mr. Groome as not the Plamen but the Oganj. You were unable to even see those -- well, rather, big differences. What makes you now so confident in knowing all kind of details if it's not to millimetres then at least in centimetres and construction and whatever?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My knowledge about multiple-rocket launchers is limited. I've pointed that out several times. My basic knowledge about this is that the Plamen has 32 rockets and that the other rocket systems have less and longer barrels, and I think that I didn't say anything different beforehand. So the only difference is that here we see some new systems that I am not familiar with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. You're not familiar with the systems you see now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I've already said that I saw the Plamen system firing, and I saw it on photographs, television, and so on. I know that this system has 32 rockets, and I know that there are several versions of this system that were made, and I know that the Oganj system has less rockets but they have a longer range. This is the basic knowledge that I have about these systems.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now having reviewed these photographs both by the Prosecution and the ones we've just gone through, what is your recollection of the type of rocket engines that were used for the three aerial bombs launched by your brigade?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that Plamen rocket systems were used.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And are you familiar with -- that is, have you heard of a weapon system called the BM-21 Grad?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just superficially. But I know that this is a rocket system that has rockets that are a lot longer and the range is longer, but the principle according to which it functions is the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Between the Plamen and the Oganj system, how did the rockets compare in size?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
